description: Indices represent the base and exponent of numbers. Surds are irrational roots that cannot be expressed as rational numbers. This study guide covers all crucial rules, formulas, and comparison methods required for competitive exams.

sections.title: Laws of Indices
sections.description: When a number is multiplied by itself repeatedly, it is expressed using indices (or exponents). These laws help in simplifying complex exponential expressions.

equations: a^0 = 1 (where a is not equal to 0)

key_concepts.explanation: Here, 'a' is the base being multiplied, and 'n' is the exponent (or index) which indicates how many times the base is multiplied by itself.

sections.title: Surds and its Types
sections.description: A surd is an irrational root of a rational number that cannot be further simplified into a whole number or a clean fraction.

key_concepts.explanation: A surd which has no rational factor other than 1. The entire value resides strictly inside the radical sign.
A surd that consists of a rational factor multiplied by an irrational factor.

sections.title: Rationalization
sections.description: The mathematical process of eliminating a surd or irrational number from the denominator of a fraction.

steps.title: Identify the Conjugate
steps.detail: If the denominator is √a + √b, its conjugate is √a - √b. Simply reverse the middle sign.

steps.title: Multiply Numerator and Denominator
steps.detail: Multiply both the top and bottom of the fraction by the identified conjugate to maintain the fraction's original value.

steps.title: Simplify
steps.detail: Use the algebraic identity (x+y)(x-y) = x^2 - y^2 in the denominator to convert it into a rational number.

sections.title: Comparison of Surds and Indices
sections.description: Specific techniques for determining the largest or smallest value among a given set of large powers or complex roots.

steps.title: Equalize the order of surds
steps.detail: When comparing surds, find the Least Common Multiple (LCM) of the orders of all the given roots and convert them into the same order.

steps.title: Find HCF for indices
steps.detail: When comparing numbers with large powers, find the Highest Common Factor (HCF) of the exponents and divide the powers by the HCF to simplify them.

results: The HCF of the powers (60, 48, 36) is 12.
Compare the resulting base values: 32, 81, and 64.
The LCM of the orders (2, 3, 4) is 12.
